'''Damieon Dante Hall''' (born September 20, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]] for nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He is nicknamed "'''the Human Joystick'''" and "'''the X-Factor'''".<ref name="Bears' Hester Emerges From the Tall Grass">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/01/sports/football/01hester.html?n=Top/News/Sports/Pro%20Football/National%20Football%20League/Chicago%20Bears|title=Bears' Hester Emerges From the Tall Grass|access-date=June 18, 2008 | work=The New York Times | first=Lee | last=Jenkins | date=February 1, 2007}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]] and was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the fifth round of the [[2000 NFL draft]]. Hall played for the Chiefs for seven years before being traded to the [[St. Louis Rams]] in 2007.<ref name="Ramstrade">{{cite web |url= https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2848789|title= Rams deal fifth-round pick for Hall|access-date=February 3, 2008 |work= ESPN|date= April 25, 2007}}</ref> Hall was ranked the 10th greatest return specialist in NFL history on [[NFL Network]]'s [[NFL Top 10]] Return Aces. He was inducted into the [[Missouri Sports Hall of Fame]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dante Hall – Missouri Sports Hall of Fame |url=https://mosportshalloffame.com/inductees/dante-hall/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He played for the [[Buffalo Bills]] from 1995 to 1998, [[Green Bay Packers]] in 1998 and [[Indianapolis Colts]] in 1999.

Holmes attended [[John Muir High School]] in Pasadena and then [[Pasadena City College]] before playing [[college football]] for the [[Portland State Vikings football|Portland State Vikings]].

In that postseason, he had 15 rushes for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' first playoff game against the [[Miami Dolphins]].  In the next game, against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], he had four rushes for 14 yards.  In 1996, he played in 16 games and had 189 rushing attempts for 571 yards (3.0 yards per carry) and had four touchdowns.  He also had 16 receptions for 102 yards (6.4 yards per reception) and had one receiving touchdown.  In the Bills' postseason game against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] Holmes had nine rushes for 10 yards and one reception for eleven yards.  In 1997, he played in thirteen games.  He had 22 rushing attempts for 106 yards (4.8 yards per carry) and had two touchdowns.  He had 13 receptions for 106 yards (8.2 yards per reception) as well.  He had 23 kick returns for 430 yards (18.7 yards per return).  In 1998, he played in three games and had two carries for 8 yards (4.0 yards per carry).  He also had one 9 yard reception.  Holmes returned one kick for twenty yards.  Later in 1998, Darick signed with the Packers. In 1999, Holmes became a free agent again and signed with the Colts.  He played in one game and had no action.
